name: 旭川成吉思汗 大黒屋 新宿駅東口店 (Asahikawa Jingisukan Daikokuya Shinjuku Stat)

claims.text: The retail 'Daikokuya-supervised' Jingisukan sauce (same brand/recipe lineage as the restaurant's tare), made by Sorachi, lists ingredients including soy sauce (国内製造), apple, sugar, hydrolyzed protein, onion, rice fermentation seasoning, vinegar, spices, sake, salt, kelp extract, bonito extract, and states it contains wheat, soy, chicken, pork, and apple.

name: 浅草 熟成味噌らーめん のりあき・美々 (Asakusa Jukusei Miso Ramen Noriaki Bibi)

claims.text: The signature soup is a pork bone and chicken based broth blended with aged miso, and standard toppings include pork chashu and pork back fat plus a soy-marinated egg — no plant-based broth, protein, or vegetarian/vegan option is mentioned in any coverage of the shop.

name: 浅草もんじゃお好み焼き ぽんちゃん (Asakusa Monja Okonomiyaki Ponchan)

claims.text: The menu includes a vegetable-forward monjayaki positioned as a lighter, healthier option, though this is a marketing description rather than a confirmed vegan or allergen-free dish.

name: 浅草おにぎりはるちゃん (Asakusa Onigiri Haruchan)

claims.text: No dedicated gluten-free preparation area or protocol was found in any source; the menu's karaage (fried chicken) and soy-sauce-based fillings suggest wheat is present in the kitchen, creating cross-contact risk for celiac diners.
One listed filling is 卵黄しょうゆ漬け (soy-sauce-marinated egg yolk), and standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat unless specifically labeled tamari/gluten-free.

The core menu is built around fish (salmon, mentaiko/cod roe), egg, and meat-based sides (tonjiru pork soup, karaage fried chicken), so shared rice, utensils, and cooking surfaces are not confirmed free of animal-product contact even for a plain rice ball.
The shop's signature ramen broth uses standard Yamasa soy sauce, the same wheat-containing shoyu the original 1910 shop used, rather than a gluten-free/tamari alternative.

name: お好み焼 鉄板焼 つる次郎（浅草 つる次郎 本店） (Asakusa Tsurujiro (Okonomiyaki Teppanyaki Ts)

claims.text: The restaurant's showcased dashi is made from whole chicken simmered with vegetables over three days, and this broth underlies the okonomiyaki/monjayaki batter — meaning the core dish is not vegan by default and cannot simply be made vegan by omitting toppings.

name: アジアンダイニング&バー SAPANA 水道橋店 (Asian Dining & Bar SAPANA Suidobashi)

claims.text: A vegetarian set is offered, including samosas, a spinach-cheese curry, a vegetable curry, salad, and a choice of naan or rice.

name: ベーカリー サンチノ 渋谷店 (Bakery Santino Shibuya)

claims.text: The bread's dough is a blend of rice flour and a small amount of intentionally-added wheat gluten (~20% of the flour blend) for texture and rise — this is a general-purpose bakery producing rice-and-wheat-gluten breads together, not a dedicated gluten-free facility, and it is explicitly described as 'not completely gluten-free.'
The shop is well regarded as an approachable option for people curious about rice-flour bread's moist texture, though coverage is careful to note it is not a strict gluten-free product.
